Veradermics has announced positive results from the Phase III trial of the VDPHL01 tablet for baldness.

Veradermics reported that the prolonged-release minoxidil tablet VDPHL01 met all primary and secondary endpoints in the Phase III study. The trial involved 536 men with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia.
According to the company's data, differences from placebo in hair counts, patient assessments, and investigator evaluations were seen as early as two months. By six months, non-vellus hair growth per square centimeter was 28.6 with once-daily dosing and 36.4 with twice-daily dosing compared to 6.6 with placebo. The developers stated that no serious adverse events related to the drug or cardiac events were reported.

The company plans to submit an application for approval to the FDA. If approved, this would be the first non-hormonal oral treatment for androgenetic alopecia.

📌 Atomic Swaps: Exchanging Crypto Without Trusting an Intermediary

Main Points
⏺ Atomic swaps allow participants to exchange assets without handing funds to a centralized custodian
⏺ The mechanism is designed so both sides receive their assets or the exchange doesn't complete
⏺ This post explains why atomic swaps are an interesting approach to decentralized trading

1️⃣ Core Idea — two users want to exchange assets from different blockchains without trusting an exchange or intermediary with their funds.
2️⃣ How It Works — one approach uses cryptographic secrets and time restrictions to coordinate an exchange under predefined rules.
3️⃣ Main Advantage — participants don't need to transfer custody of their assets to a third party during the exchange.
4️⃣ The Challenges — networks need compatible mechanisms, while participants need liquidity, time, and correct execution.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — before swapping, review fees on both chains, lock periods, technical requirements, and refund conditions.

Final Thoughts

Atomic swaps aim to solve a fundamental crypto problem: how to exchange value with a stranger without relying on their honesty.

📌 Hyperliquid adds 10 HYPE rule as price falls to $78.98 

🔗 Hyperliquid has introduced revised order priority rules on its testnet, including a reported 10 HYPE delegation requirement for traders seeking faster order handling through its priority fee system. In an October 18 announcement circulated through its community channels, the decentralized derivatives platform outlined changes to write priority fees following feedback from users. The proposed rules concern traders who depend on low delays when placing, modifying or canceling orders.

🔖 The announcement identifies four changes involving account settings, transaction processing and eligibility for priority fees. Hyperliquid’s existing technical documentation confirms how its priority fee system operates, although the newly reported delegation threshold has not yet appeared in the publicly accessible documentation reviewed for this report. The changes are described as live on testnet. No confirmed date has been announced for applying the revised requirements to mainnet trading.

‼️ The October 18 update introduces a minimum delegated balance of 10 HYPE for accounts seeking to use IOC and ALO priority fees, according to the announcement. IOC, short for immediate-or-cancel, refers to an order that attempts immediate execution and cancels any portion that cannot be filled. ALO, or add-liquidity-only, is used to place orders that join the order book without immediately taking available liquidity.

Strikes against these sites might disrupt Tehran’s ability to launch attacks and impose substantial economic costs. But the destruction of infrastructure does not automatically eliminate the technical expertise, industrial networks, or political determination needed to rebuild it. That uncertainty is central to the debate in Washington.

A limited campaign could produce visible military results without resolving the underlying confrontation. A broader offensive might inflict more damage but also provoke a response that neither the United States nor Israel could easily contain. 

Iran could retaliate against Israeli territory, American military installations, or regional partners, while attacks on shipping could threaten the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most strategically important energy corridors.

The economic consequences could reach far beyond the Middle East. Any serious disruption to oil shipments or regional energy infrastructure could drive prices higher, intensifying inflationary pressure in the United States and elsewhere. For Trump, that would create a stark contradiction: a military campaign designed to improve American and allied security could simultaneously raise costs for consumers and undermine confidence in his economic agenda.

Gil Murciano, chief executive of the Israeli Institute for Regional Foreign Policies, has also pointed to the domestic political constraints surrounding the conflict. The unpopularity of military action among American voters, he argues, complicates the prospect of a new escalation before the midterm elections. That political reality does not eliminate the risk of war, but it may influence the timing and scale of any decision.

Meanwhile, diplomacy remains fragile. Washington may believe that the threat of renewed strikes can force Tehran to compromise on its nuclear program and regional activities. Iran, however, could interpret the same preparations as evidence that negotiations offer little protection against future attacks. 

If that perception hardens, military pressure could narrow the diplomatic space rather than expand it. The most dangerous possibility is that neither side intends to trigger a full-scale regional war, yet both continue taking steps that make one increasingly difficult to avoid. 

A miscalculation, an attack causing significant casualties, or a sudden disruption to shipping could rapidly change the calculations in Washington, Jerusalem, and Tehran. For now, the military plans represent preparation, not a confirmed order to attack. 

Trump could still decide that diplomatic pressure offers a better path than another campaign. But as military exercises intensify and negotiations remain uncertain, the region is entering a period in which even a limited incident could carry consequences far beyond its immediate target. 

The real test for Washington and Jerusalem will not simply be whether they can strike Iran again. It will be whether they have a credible strategy for what comes afterward. 

Without a clear political endgame, another offensive could destroy infrastructure, deepen regional instability, and leave the central conflict unresolved. The question hanging over the Middle East is no longer just how a new war might begin, but whether anyone can guarantee where it would end.

⚠️ Tether leads $15M funding for Mural to power AI agent payments 

👀 Tether has led a $15 million Series A funding round for New York-based Mural, supporting the financial technology company’s development of payment infrastructure for businesses and artificial intelligence agents. Mural plans to use the investment to expand internationally and develop the banking, payment and compliance services needed for software agents to conduct financial transactions.

🔔 Founded in 2022 by former Palantir engineers Sinclair Toffa and Chris Fernandes, the company provides infrastructure that businesses use to manage accounts, payment instructions, identity verification and regulatory requirements across banking networks and blockchains. Its customers include global payroll provider Deel, browser developer Opera and financial technology platform Axexo. Through Mural’s system, businesses can offer accounts holding dollars, local currencies and stablecoins without managing separate financial infrastructure for each payment method.

📌 The company reported processing $2.1 billion in payments for users across 128 countries since introducing its application programming interface in 2025. Payment volume recorded so far in 2026 is nearly six times its total for 2025. Mural has not disclosed the valuation attached to the latest funding round. Fortune reported that the company previously raised $5 million in seed financing in 2022, followed by additional capital from existing backers.
